:::{#def-vector-sequence-limit}
#### Iterates and convergence of a sequence of vectors

A [sequence](sets-functions.qmd#def-sequence) $\vx^{(0)}, \vx^{(1)}, \ldots$ in $\reals^p$
**converges** to $\vx^* \in \reals^p$
if the sequence of distances $\norm{\vx^{(t)} - \vx^*}$
[converges](algebra.qmd#def-sequence-limit) to $0$.
For $p = 1$, $\norm{x^{(t)} - x^*} = \abs{x^{(t)} - x^*}$,
and this is the convergence of a sequence of numbers to $x^*$.

An **iterative method** starts from a point $\vx^{(0)}$
and computes $\vx^{(t+1)}$ from $\vx^{(t)}$ by a fixed rule, for $t = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$;
the points $\vx^{(t)}$ are its **iterates**.
For a point $\vx^*$ that the method is meant to reach,
$\norm{\vx^{(t)} - \vx^*}$ is the **error** of the iterate $\vx^{(t)}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-vector-sequence-limit}
#### Halving a vector

The iterative method $\vx^{(t+1)} = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\vx^{(t)}$ from $\vx^{(0)} = \tp{(4, 2)}$
has iterates $\tp{(4, 2)}, \tp{(2, 1)}, \tp{(1, 0.5)}, \ldots$,
that is, $\vx^{(t)} = 2^{-t}\,\tp{(4, 2)}$.
With $\vx^* = \vzero$, the error of $\vx^{(t)}$ is

$$
\ba
\norm{2^{-t}\,\tp{(4, 2)} - \vzero}
&= 2^{-t}\,\norm{\tp{(4, 2)}}
&& \text{(norm of a multiple)}
\\
&= 2^{-t} \sqrt{20},
&& \text{(} 4^2 + 2^2 = 20 \text{)}
\ea
$$

which converges to $0$, so the iterates converge to $\vzero$.

:::
